This study presents a novel semi-supervised non-negative canonical matrix factorization (CNMF) method designed for piano transcription that leverages a minimal amount of labeled audio data. While recent deep learning approaches for this task have achieved impressive results, they remain heavily dependent on vast datasets for training. To address this limitation, we propose a framework that integrates a data-driven Dirichlet prior with a deep generative model trained using very sparse annotations in a self-supervised manner. For transcription using new audio, we then employ a conventional CNMF algorithm and initialize it with the parameters derived from the generative model. Experimental results indicate that this semi-supervised CNMF approach outperforms both current state-of-the-art low-rank factorization techniques and supervised deep learning pipelines for piano transcription using minimal labeled data.

We investigate the thermodynamic and geometric consistency of modeling stellar rotation via general-relativistic (GR) fluid elements. While standard literature assigns macroscopic quantities like mass and specific angular momentum directly to fluid elements, we demonstrate that such a framework necessitates a well-defined geometry and state relations for those elements. In the context of fluid elements as fundamental thermodynamic entities, this implies that mass and specific angular momentum cannot be arbitrarily chosen; rather, they must be linked by constitutive relations. We further establish that for a barotropic star, a unique geometric configuration arises from any specific set of fluid element constitutive relations. This induced geometric structure allows us to derive the hydrodynamic equilibrium equations directly as conditions on the parameters defining the fluid element constitutive relations. Finally, we analyze several instances of these constitutive relations and compute the corresponding equilibrium stellar configurations.

Acquiring labeled data is often costly, yet most data labeling protocols require selecting only the most informative samples for human review. Selective labeling serves as a critical strategy to maximize the performance of machine learning models by minimizing reliance on labeled datasets. In this paper, we present a fresh approach to selective labeling grounded in a new concept called "mutual information between samples." This concept is derived from the standard multivariate Gaussian assumption typically made in model-centric methods. By contrasting this with established techniques, we demonstrate that our proposed approach yields a broader set of informative samples, resulting in superior overall model accuracy.

The merger of two neutron stars generates both gravitational and electromagnetic waves, serving as a unique scenario for studying fundamental physics and the interplay of electromagnetic and gravitational radiations. In this work, we calculate the gravitational and electromagnetic radiation produced by a neutron star merger within the linear approximation, utilizing a formalism that facilitates the conversion between the time-domain and frequency-domain representations. Our findings indicate that in the frequency domain, the gravitational and electromagnetic strains are decoupled, allowing them to be analyzed independently. Conversely, in the time-domain formulation, the strains remain intrinsically linked. We further demonstrate that incorporating electromagnetic data into gravitational wave analyses can enhance the accuracy of parameter estimation regarding the emitted radiation. Consequently, future multi-messenger observations of strongly interacting neutron star mergers in the time domain are essential for capturing the coupled nature of gravitational and electromagnetic strains and for fully exploiting the scientific potential of combined radiation signals.

Social determinants of health (SDOH) are critical to patient well-being, yet the information documenting them is often unstructured and dispersed across electronic health records (EHRs). This study introduces an automated system designed to identify and extract SDOH from clinical notes, leveraging a combination of Named Entity Recognition (NER) and text classification models. The necessary labels for training were created by coding SDOH-related terms found in existing literature. Validation of the proposed label set was achieved using a separate test set of EHR notes, while the extraction algorithms were evaluated on both annotated notes and free-text search inputs containing queries about a patient's SDOH. The results demonstrate that the proposed label schema is robust and that the proposed approach is feasible and effective.

We examine a swimmer held at fixed positions in a two-dimensional fluid at large scales, subject to a time-periodic flow field that periodically switches frequency. The analysis quantifies how this swimming cost varies with the switching frequency. By demonstrating that two distinct spatial regions form behind the swimmer—each governed by a different dynamical regime—we show that as the switching frequency increases, the total cost behaves linearly. Furthermore, at low frequencies, the cost is minimized by rapidly moving the swimmer between regions. This optimal strategy involves a trade-off: it balances the additional energy required to reposition the swimmer against the energy saved by avoiding the more expensive, persistent dynamical regime.

Urban environments typically foster a diverse array of encounters that foster community resilience; however, the pandemic likely diminished such encounters in cities for an extended duration, with its lingering impacts remaining largely unexamined. Drawing on data from 1.5 million geotagged social media posts collected between March 2020 and February 2021 across the United States, this study examines the durability of pandemic-related reductions in urban visitation diversity two years post-onset. Our findings indicate that such diversity took at least two years to recover to pre-pandemic levels, with full recovery delayed by an additional month for every 1,000 inhabitants per square kilometer. This temporal disparity suggests that while individual return patterns normalized within 18 months, the aggregate diversity of urban visits remained significantly altered for a longer stretch, with higher-density areas experiencing more pronounced and enduring disruptions. These results highlight the necessity of extended monitoring and underscore the importance of urban planning strategies designed to facilitate varied and safe interactions, recognizing that the societal footprint of the crisis extends well beyond its immediate timeline.

The presence of migrating bodies within circumstellar discs can significantly alter a disc's internal structure. Using three-dimensional Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations, we examined the impact of both migrating objects and their outflows on the inner regions of a high-mass (10 $M_{\odot}$) radiatively cooled protoplanetary disc surrounding a young stellar object. Our findings indicate that migrating bodies induce a distinct density trough near the migration origin, leading to an increase in specific angular momentum for the innermost material. This alteration causes the inner disc to migrate and enhances the coupling between the inner and outer regions, allowing outer disturbances to influence the inner dynamics. Furthermore, the outflows of migrating objects can restructure the disc by clearing gaps and depositing new material, thereby altering the inner disc's composition. These results suggest that the innermost parts of circumstellar discs are shaped not only by the star's radiation but also by migrating bodies and their outflows.

This manuscript outlines the fundamental components required to define a scattering theory: specifically, the asymptotic algebra, the scattering matrix, and the corresponding unitary implementation. We examine free scalar field theory in d+1 dimensional Minkowski spacetime, identifying its asymptotic algebra and calculating the associated scattering matrix. Additionally, we analyze several cases of static spacetimes featuring a single asymptotically flat region, deriving their respective asymptotic algebras, scattering matrices, and unitary realizations. These cases include the Schwarzschild metric and a simplified model representing a d-dimensional spacetime containing a spherical cavity. Leveraging the derived asymptotic algebras and scattering matrices, we subsequently address the construction of charged quantization within both asymptotically flat Schwarzschild and cavity-containing scenarios.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for evaluating 5G cellular exposure, grounded in the spatial distribution of buildings and the 5G Non-Statistical (NS) Exposure Model. While the original NS model relies on site-specific parameters, this study adapts it for use in exposure assessments by deriving these parameters through a Monte Carlo simulation based on building distribution datasets. The assessment methodology was validated using building attenuation data from Germany, revealing that 5G base station exposure is significantly influenced by local cellular network configurations and building data. Crucially, the study demonstrates that attenuation from buildings with planar interfaces results in higher exposure levels compared to attenuation models for horn-shaped or pyramidal structures. Furthermore, exposure from towers utilizing Small-Medium Medium-Medium-Medium (SMMS) antennas is calculated to be approximately 10 to 20 times greater than that from traditional large towers. Finally, the research establishes that exposure from 5G cellular towers is largely contingent upon the specific 5G attenuation model selected and the local building inventory.

This study addresses the free surface problem for two-dimensional, incompressible, irrotational water waves with finite depth. It examines a novel, robust surface reconstruction technique applicable to both periodic and localized scenarios. For periodic waves, the method leverages the fact that the Fourier modes of the potential at the surface match those of the envelope, allowing inversion via a linear system derived from an envelope approximation near the deep water limit. For localized waves, the approach utilizes energy conservation and far-field asymptotic analysis to determine surface elevation.

This is a new, original proof of the surface layer theorem, which is also known as the Brouwer-Santall lemma. It states that for every non-constant differential form $\omega$ of degree $k \ge k$ in a bounded, open set $U \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, there exists a bounded, open set $V \subset U$ such that $\omega$ is exact on $V$ if and only if $\omega$ is exact on $U$. This theorem has been applied to establish a new result in the theory of differential forms within bounded, open sets in finite dimensional spaces that are locally convex.

This study introduces a novel navigation system leveraging sonar sensors to enhance mobile robots. The proposed layered control architecture consists of three distinct levels: perception, decision-making, and execution. At the decision-making level, a set of reactive behaviors is established to determine navigation actions. To facilitate this, the perception level utilizes a new algorithm for data processing that eliminates the need for complex calibration. Finally, the execution level executes these decisions by directly commanding the robot's actuators. Experimental results confirm the system's efficacy in navigating unstructured environments while successfully detecting and avoiding obstacles.

This study introduces two models, HFNER and ContextFNER, which leverage contextual data to enhance the accuracy of fake news source detection. These sources are often characterized as misleading falsehoods disseminated through social media. The HFNER model utilizes a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) architecture, trained on the Fake News Detection 2018 dataset. In contrast, ContextFNER improves upon HFNER by integrating an attention mechanism to process additional contextual information, specifically the most upvoted comments associated with fake news items. ContextFNER functions as an advanced iteration of HFNER, trained on the same dataset but incorporating these comments to achieve superior results. Evaluations demonstrate that both models significantly outperform the baseline rule-based approach, with ContextFNER delivering the highest accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores.

This study examines the impact of curvature on the phase transition within a binary white emulsion consisting of droplets stabilized by surfactants. We analyze the free energy landscape across various states to determine the conditions for a transition between the single and triple droplet configurations. Our findings indicate that increasing the system's curvature—achieved by placing the emulsion in smaller spherical confinement—triggers the transition by maximizing curvature-induced entropy, a rise driven specifically by interfacial fluctuations. This entropic mechanism challenges conventional theories which attribute such transition to minimization of interfacial energy. Furthermore, we demonstrate that increasing curvature enhances the transition's first-order character, evidenced by the amplification of the free energy barrier, hysteresis, and the magnitude of interfacial tension disjoining.

This paper evaluates a suboptimal decoding order policy that selects a subset of users for successive cancellation graph (SC-graph) decoding. By deriving the probability distribution of block error rates under this scheme, we demonstrate how to optimize the system's sum rate. Furthermore, we introduce a new method for designing SC-graphs. Our proposed decoding orders yield performance that closely matches the theoretically optimal sum rate, yet they substantially lower computational complexity. Specifically, the optimal complexity is reduced to $O(2^{K/2}K^K)$, compared to the $O(2^KK^K)$ required for the optimal design, where $K$ represents the number of users.

We introduce a novel, solvable relaxation of the concave two-variable expression representing rotationally invariant L1-PCA, enabling its resolution via alternating l1-minimization. Although three specific variational forms are derived, only the first facilitates a tractable two-lagrange multipliers optimization scheme, whereas the second and third lead to three-multiplier problems that preclude this specific approach. Numerical evaluations confirm that an optimization algorithm based on the first formulation converges to a solution superior to the current state-of-the-art heuristics for the two-variable L1-PCA variant.

We introduce a self-supervised method for refining semantic labeling datasets that eliminates label inconsistencies by utilizing paraphrasing tasks as a means to validate annotated labels through re-labeling instances using paraphrases of the original descriptions. In this approach, paraphrases serve as new labels for existing images. By training a segmentation model on these labeled images with paraphrase-based labels, we can subsequently infer instance masks from images that only have their descriptions rephrased. If two descriptions for the same image are paraphrases of each other, a correctly functioning segmentation model should ideally produce identical masks when processed with either description. Discrepancies in the generated masks indicate a contradiction between the original and paraphrased labels, allowing us to identify and filter out such inconsistent annotations. We implemented this self-supervised framework using the ADE20K dataset, which resulted in a dataset with enhanced quality. Furthermore, we observed improved segmentation model metrics when trained on the cleaned dataset compared to those trained on the unmodified dataset.

A prefix-independent positional winning condition has been introduced and demonstrated to be equivalent to the conjunction of up to two prefix-independent half-positional conditions. It is also shown that the most accurate approximation using a half-positional condition for a given such condition is formed by the union of no more than two such conjuncts, with the number of components in this conjunction bounded by the specific structure of the original condition. Furthermore, it is determined that the union of two prefix-independent half-positional conditions is guaranteed to be equivalent to some prefix-independent positional condition, whereas the approximation suggests this limit cannot be extended, as the union of three or more such half-positional conditions can yield a result that is not equivalent to any single half-positional condition.

This study presents observations of the X-ray spectra for the asynchronous polar RS Iri, collected by XMM-Newton on May 19, 2012, and June 10, 2013. Following a detailed spectral analysis, we compared our findings with those of the standard polar, PSR B1957+20, obtained under identical instrumental conditions. The spectral comparison methodology involved fitting both datasets with the same set of thermal and non-thermal components, allowing the flux of the non-thermal component in the RS Iri spectrum to remain unconstrained. Results indicate that the non-thermal component flux in the RS Iri spectrum is significantly higher than in the PSR B1957+20 spectrum, with a flux ratio of approximately 10. Furthermore, the electron temperature associated with this component in RS Iri exceeds that in PSR B1957+20 by a factor of roughly 3.6. These outcomes suggest that the non-thermal emission characteristics of the magnetic pole in the RS Iri spectrum are markedly different from those observed in typical polar stars.

This study examines fluid-structure interaction (FSI) problems using a fluid domain decomposition method. Specifically, the current work focuses on fluid partitioning where subdomains are separated by a master-slave interface. The fluid and solid sub-problems are formulated and solved independently, with the fluid domain decomposition technique managing the fluid domain. The method relies on a high-order, body-fitted grid generation approach to define the decomposition interfaces. On one side lies a fluid domain, and on the other a solid domain, with the method ensuring continuity of displacement across the interface while maintaining fluid subdomain mass conservation. Convergence is established through a strong coupling strategy, in which the fluid and solid solutions are iteratively resolved until a converged solution is achieved. Numerical tests confirm the method's accuracy and convergence, demonstrating results for both a compliant valve scenario and a fluid domain decomposition test case.

To address the issue of memory inefficiency in standard metric maps, which suffer by storing every possible state equally, we introduce HiTMap, a navigation-centric global representation that uses learned policies to prioritize and store only the most critical map entries. By leveraging sparse reinforcement learning, our method populates the map selectively based on navigational significance. Our experiments demonstrate that robots utilizing HiTMap navigate 1000 times more environments than those using conventional Global Metric Maps, while maintaining performance that is virtually indistinguishable in terms of path length and travel time.

This paper details the development of a system that utilizes deep learning to identify and categorify abusive Twitter posts based on the 2019 Abusive Content Challenge (ACC-19). Held as a industry-academia partnership by Twitter and TCS iSystems, this challenge focused on four primary tasks: binary detection of abuse, multiclass classification of abuse types, summarizing non-abusive tweets, and identifying accounts that frequently post abuse. Our team achieved a macro $F_1$-score of 63.64% for the detection task and 50.59% for the classification task. Our methodology leverages TCS iSystems' vast repository of over 50 million manually annotated tweets, combined with an additional 1.45 million augmented annotations created through a state-of-the-art generative adversarial network (GAN) framework. These robust datasets were used to train our system using various neural architectures, including Bidirectional Encoder Representations from TCS iSystems (BERT), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs). Furthermore, we conducted an extensive ablation study to analyze the efficacy of different annotation levels, diverse data splits, and the specific contributions of our GAN-based augmentation strategy. In total, this effort represents a significant push toward safer social media environments through advanced automated moderation.

Atomic interferometry has recently enabled the detection of local magnetic fields with extreme sensitivity, potentially reaching $10^{-14}\,\text{T}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ ($10$ nG/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$). This exceptional sensitivity arises from the ability to average out both intrinsic magnetic field fluctuations and those generated by imperfect active shielding. However, existing studies have not adequately assessed the feasibility of this technique for specific applications, such as mapping fields in MRI suites. To address this gap, we propose a new analytical model for calculating the spatial sensitivity of local field detection in atomic interferometry. Applying this model to determine the suitability of these measurements for mapping residual field fluctuations in an MRI room demonstrates that detection sensitivities as low as $50$ pT/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ ($5$ nG/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$) are achievable within a $10$ cm$\times$10 cm area.

We introduce a conceptually straightforward magnetothermoelectric device built from a spin-filtering heterostructure, such as one composed of graphene on NiO. This system leverages the distinct magnetocaloric responses of majority and minority spin carriers to generate opposing heating or cooling effects—warming one spin channel while cooling the other—at a single location. Consequently, the device facilitates selective magnetothermoelectric power generation, yielding currents with identical temperatures but opposite chemical potentials. Furthermore, by adjusting the magnetocaloric strength, it is possible to transition from two opposite thermally induced voltages to none at all, effectively creating a magnetic-field-tunable Seebeck coefficient that crosses zero. This behavior mirrors the standard thermoelectric transition observed when a semiconductor's carrier type shifts from $n$-type to $p$-type across its critical doping level. Analogously, in our spin-filtering architecture, the tunable magnetocaloric effect surpasses the standard spin-dependent magnetization contribution, dominating the overall response. Finally, we propose a magnetic-field-controlled pump mechanism capable of transferring heat between spin streams, resulting in a net temperature difference where one spin population heats up and the other cools down.

This study introduces a straightforward and adaptable methodology for incorporating non-local gap effects into a comprehensive model of light propagation through disordered media. While standard local theories like the diffusion approximation or the Bethe-Salpaut equation accurately predict general transport metrics—such as the diffusion coefficient and mean free path—they fail to capture specific features of the transmission spectrum, including the spectral second peak and the interference fringe structure, when the gap between disorderly regions is small. In contrast, our proposed effective gap width approach yields highly accurate results for gap sizes down to zero, closely matching both numerical simulations and the experimentally observed regime. Furthermore, this framework reliably forecasts key non-local spectral attributes, specifically the weight and positioning of the subdiffusive peak and fringe characteristics, aligning well with established theories of non-locality. computationally, this model demands significantly fewer resources than advanced non-local schemes, presenting a robust tool for analyzing light propagation in gap systems.

The calculus of constructions, introduced by Bertrand Castéran in 1987, stands as a pinnacle in type theory history, profoundly shaping subsequent developments and earning recognition as a major force in the evolution of the field. Despite its profound impact on later systems like Agda and Coq, extensive formal work within the calculus of constructions itself remains relatively scarce compared to these derivatives. This paper introduces a formalization of the calculus of constructions within the Coq proof assistant, designed to support ongoing research efforts. By implementing core functionalities such as an interactive theorem prover, type checker, and conversion engine, this implementation serves as a flexible testbed. Researchers can utilize it to explore specific aspects of type theory and perform critical analyses, such as examining the decidability of conversion in the context of the 3-coherent structures.

New paradigms in quantum electronics are emerging, with the concept of entanglement serving as a central driver. This paper demonstrates these innovations using a single-electron box as a model system. We evaluate two specific methods for quantifying entanglement—the correlator approach and the von-Neumann density-matrix technique—highlighting their utility in understanding quantum electronic behaviors. Furthermore, we explore how these boxes function as quantum switches and examine their application to a two-electron version that generates a specific type of non-classical current known as blockade current. Finally, the study assesses the system's resilience against noise, a critical metric for developing stable quantum technologies.

Population-level admixture inference is increasingly applied to identify the population-level history of species. This research suggests that applying population-level selection pressure to detect shifts in these dynamics is equally valuable. We demonstrate that standard admixture models, which are sensitive to the number of clusters, can be improved by using a Dirichlet process prior on the admixture proportions themselves. This methodological choice allows for the recovery of distinct, identifiable selection-driven admixture shifts across genomic landscapes. Our findings are illustrated through genomic data from *Drosophila melanogaster*, revealing identifiable selection-driven shifts in hybridization dynamics across the species' range under varying migration regimes. This approach offers a robust framework for analyzing how admixture is selected upon in hybridizing populations. This paper examines variable stepsize multilevel Miller-Rosenbloom (SGLMs) within the context of nonuniform grid systems, specifically analyzing their bias characteristics and convergence rates. Our approach involves applying techniques of operator expansion on the associated linear differential operator to derive a bias expansion for the scheme. These analytical tools were used to investigate how variable stepsize SGLMs behave on both uniform and nonuniform grids. While it has already been established that variable stepsize SGLMs exhibit second-order convergence on uniform grids with bias coefficients of $O(h^2)$, our analysis demonstrates that on general smooth, positive, smooth grid functions, the bias is of order $O(h)$, resulting in first-order convergence ($O(h)$). This represents a notable distinction from the uniform case, where the bias coefficient is of order $h^2$. To address this reduction, we propose a specific grid function that yields a bias coefficient of $h^2$, thereby restoring second-order convergence. Numerical results are provided to confirm these theoretical findings.

The Multivariate Functional Subspace Superimposition Analysis (MFSSA) serves as a versatile framework designed to handle various joint problems involving time-series data and multivariate functions. This section demonstrates MFSSA's application through two specific instances: analyzing univariate temperature curve data for multiple subjects in a classification task, and addressing multivariate remote sensing image superimposition analysis by forecasting future multivariate imagery based on historical records. These examples highlight MFSSA's capability to effectively manage both univariate time series classification and multivariate functional forecasting in diverse real-world scenarios.

Current automatic essay scoring models that utilize deep learning are noted for two problematic traits: oversensitivity and overstability. Specifically, oversensitivity manifests as a tendency to assign disparate scores to semantically equivalent essays due to minor surface-level variations, while overstability refers to the model's rigid adherence to an initial score despite substantial changes in a reference dialogue's content. This paper investigates these characteristics from the perspective of the decision boundaries within the scoring decisions made by these systems. We posit that oversensitivity and overstability stem from specific, suboptimal decision boundaries characterized by irregularity and excessive curvature. To address this, we introduce a novel methodology for constructing decision boundaries that are both smooth and sparse. Empirical results indicate that implementing these refined boundaries leads to significant reductions in both oversensitivity and overstability. Furthermore, the study confirms that this improved model maintains high correlation with human evaluators and sustains strong discriminative capability.

This study examines a random walk defined by $S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n X_i$, where the $X_i$ are independent and identically distributed with a zero mean. We analyze the asymptotic behavior of the probability $P(\max_{1 \le k \le n} S_k \le bx_n)$ as $n \to \infty$, considering two cases: when the variance is finite ($x_n = \sqrt{n}$) and when variance is infinite ($x_n = U^{-1}(n)$, with $U$ being the slowly varying inverse of the tail of the distribution of $-\min(X_1, -X_2)$). In both scenarios, the term $1-b^2$ appears as an exponent, with the parameter $b$ ranging in $(0, 1)$, serving as a critical factor in the asymptotic formulas. These results are applied to derive a "law of large numbers for the random walk conditioned to stay positive," a result originally proposed by Bertacchi.

This study introduces a novel approach to the optimization of plasma sources by employing machine learning algorithms to analyze experimental data. A specific focus was placed on optimizing an inductively coupled argon plasma (ICP) utilizing data derived from electron cyclotron emission (ECE) diagnostics. Electron cyclotron emission diagnostics offer a non-invasive method for measuring plasma parameters, yet they necessitate line-of-sight integration, a factor that complicates optimization efforts. To address this, we utilized a support vector regression algorithm to model the relationship between ECE signals and plasma parameters based on existing experimental datasets. This modeling facilitated the optimization of key parameters, specifically electron temperature ($T_e$) and density ($n_e$), using profiling data. Furthermore, the developed optimization framework was extended to plasma parameters characterized by spatially resolved electron temperature and density profiles. We demonstrate the efficacy of this methodology using data from an ICP experiment where $T_e$ and $n_e$ varied across a range of 0.5–2.5 keV and $2.5 \times 10^{19}$ to $8 \times 10^{19} \, \text{m}^{-3}$, respectively.

Controlling agricultural pests via reducing their reproductive rates is a critical challenge. This study examined the influence of entomopathogenic nematodes on the *Plutella xylostella* (diamondback moth) population, specifically analyzing their impact on the insects' mating and larval development. Experiments revealed that exposure to these nematodes significantly lowered the egg-laying capacity of adult female *P. xylostella*, resulting in fewer larvae. Furthermore, nematode exposure caused a 100% reduction in the hatching rate of the eggs that were produced. Consequently, these findings indicate that such nematodes can effectively suppress pest populations by interfering with the insects' reproductive cycles.

Nucleus segmentation serves as a vital step in numerous biomedical applications, including drug discovery, disease diagnosis, and dosage determination. Given the significant challenges posed by nucleus segmentation, researchers have increasingly turned to deep learning, with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) demonstrating remarkable efficacy in automatic nucleus detection. However, these methods often suffer from the need for extensive manual data collection and the high computational costs associated with training on massive datasets. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel, data-efficient automatic nucleus detection framework featuring a distinctive "U-shaped" architecture enhanced by a newly proposed "W-shaped" network. This design incorporates three cascaded skip connections that allow the model to retain crucial spatial information while extracting high-level semantic features. Furthermore, the framework integrates a dual-branch auxiliary detection network designed to enhance learning capabilities through the correlation of nucleus features across multiple scales. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the NuCLS dataset, surpassing existing methods by a margin of 0.5% in detection accuracy. Additionally, the study shows an improvement of approximately 0.2% in automatic detection accuracy compared to its unmodified counterpart, all while requiring only 0.5% of the training time necessary for conventional data-intensive approaches.

This paper establishes local converses for the local Langlands correspondence applicable to odd special orthogonal groups, symplectic groups, and their classical subgroups of type A. By synthesizing recent outcomes from the first and second authors regarding rank-one twists of local gamma factors with previous work by the first author and Liu concerning general twists of such factors, we achieve these primary objectives. Consequently, we derive explicit formulas that determine a family of gamma factors, thereby identifying conditions under which the local Langlands correspondence holds.

The ongoing global pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2 continues to necessitate a search for effective treatments. While these drugs must curb viral replication, they must also avoid harming host cells; specifically, they should not inadvertently trigger apoptosis, which could spark a "cytokine storm" and exacerbate disease severity. Recent research reveals that blocking the ACE2 receptor, a primary mechanism for cellular entry, induces apoptosis in host cells. Consequently, this study investigates how certain anti-inflammatory agents, which function by inhibiting the enzyme hMAO-B, interact with the viral spike protein. The findings indicate that compounds acting as hMAO-B inhibitors prevent the apoptosis triggered in ACE2-expressing cells by the spike protein. Furthermore, these drugs facilitate a transition from apoptotic to non-apoptotic necrotic cell death, a process characterized by membrane permeabilization. This suggests that pharmaceuticals capable of inhibiting hMAO-B could serve as a strategy to mitigate spike protein-induced cellular toxicity.

Algorithms designed to identify exogenous variables can mitigate the harmful effects of historical and unobserved confounding on learning outcomes by adjusting for these factors. However, these methods rely on the strict assumption that no endogenous disturbances exist, an condition that can be difficult to verify in practice. This paper introduces a novel approach to IDOL that extends existing methods to handle confounding variables when exogeneity assumptions cannot be guaranteed. The updated IDOL framework maintains the core benefits of its predecessor while ensuring robustness in identifying variables under uncertain exogeneity. Testing across both synthetic datasets and real-world applications demonstrates that the method effectively sustains high performance even in the presence of endogenous confounding.

Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for creating decentralized applications that maintain data integrity and security. Ethereum, in particular, enables the development of smart contracts using the functional programming language Ocaml via Michelson. Despite this capability, Michelson lacks a type system, which limits the ability to verify contract properties statically. To address this gap, we present HELMHOLTZ, an automated verification tool designed for Michelson. HELMHOLTZ utilizes a relational calculus to statically confirm that Michelson code adheres to soundness requirements, ensuring valid Michelson contracts. We demonstrate the tool's practical application by verifying both existing Michelson implementations and functional examples provided by the language designers.

While Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are a well-established and powerful architecture, there remains a need to clarify the fundamental principles underlying graph convolution. This study derives graph convolution from first principles, utilizing the concept of a Laplacian to determine the optimal smoothing operation that aligns with local geometric structures. Furthermore, we demonstrate that both traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and fully connected Neural Networks can be viewed as specialized instances of graph-based operations. Specifically, we show how the general framework presented here can be applied to design graph-based equivalents for standard CNN layers and dense connectivity patterns.

Finally, the entropy of a rotating hairy black hole is less than that of a standard rotating black hole with no hair in the same bulk for identical conditions.

Ultrasound elastography maps tissue mechanical properties by evaluating how ultrasound images shift under applied stress. Since ultrasound image resolution is superior in the axial direction compared to the lateral direction, elastography has historically been far more accurate for estimating axial displacement than for assessing lateral displacement. This study introduces a novel elastography-based reconstruction method that leverages the high accuracy of axial displacement estimation to improve the accuracy of the corresponding lateral displacement measurements. The approach functions by first determining the accurate axial displacement and subsequently calculating the precise location of the resulting axial strain feature along the lateral axis, where ultrasound resolution is excellent due to enhanced acoustic beamforming. Clinical trials involving liver and breast tissues demonstrate that this technique significantly improves the accuracy of lateral strain estimation by a factor of 2 to 3, while maintaining the existing accuracy for axial strain.

However, this looseness can introduce ambiguity and errors. In contrast, logical pseudocode adheres strictly to the syntax and safety constraints of a specific language, guaranteeing both correctness and security. We demonstrate its practical application by analyzing algorithms from standard algorithmic textbooks. Our findings reveal that while traditional pseudosequences often contain bugs, logical pseudosequences maintain a high degree of correctness.

Consider the Boolean lattice $2^d$ with all its subsets of $\{1, \dots, d\}$ as vertices. A $k$-rainbow monochromatic subcube of dimension $t$ arises when some $m$ elements form a subcube of dimension $t$ colored uniformly with one color $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, ensuring no other subset containing any of these $m$ elements shares that same color. We investigate the Boolean rainbow Ramsey number $\text{rainbow-RR}(2^d, \text{subcube}^t, k)$, defined as the smallest integer $N$ such that every $k$-coloring of the poweret $2^N$ guarantees a subcube of dimension $t$ colored with a $k$-rainbow instance. For the case where $k=2$, we establish the exact value of this number as $RR(2^d, \text{subcube}^t, 2) = 2^d$. Furthermore, for $k \ge 3$, we derive asymptotic lower and upper bounds for $\text{rainbow-RR}(2^d, \text{subcube}^t, k)$.

We present a one-pass coreset algorithm designed for the $k$-means clustering problem. While prior methods required knowledge of the data size ($n$) and relied on the data being streamed as a sequence, our approach functions effectively on streaming datasets where $n$ is unknown. Furthermore, this algorithm is highly practical, demanding minimal space and a single traversal of the data. Consequently, it achieves a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation using $O(\epsilon^{-2}\log k)$ times the space necessary to construct the corresponding $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate coreset.

The method also achieves performance that rivals the best centralized strategy, which requires extensive communication and computation. Our approach enables scalable decision-making for large fleets of evaders and pursuers in complex, three-dimensional marine environments by distributing the problem-solving process.

This study introduces an innovative formalism for defining quark and gluon PDFs that specifically incorporate universal corrections arising from electroweak interactions in the factorization of hadron collisions producing $W$ and $Z$ pairs. In multi-task reinforcement learning, an agent learns to handle several tasks sharing some of their environmental dynamics. While using one learned dynamics model allows agents to apply insights across tasks, it can also introduce unwanted dynamics from interfering tasks, potentially harming performance. To address this, we propose a novel approach that learns multiple dynamics models, allowing an agent to select the most appropriate one for each specific task. Our method employs a mixture of dynamics models, where the selection policy is trained via a surrogate reward function designed to maximize the total reward of all tasks. Experiments on both discrete Markov chains and continuous tasks with varying levels of stochasticity demonstrate that this approach outperforms single-model baselines. Furthermore, compared to an approach that learns distinct models for each task, our method achieves superior sample efficiency.

This paper investigates a class of differential operators defined on a noncompact manifold $M$ equipped with compact boundary $\partial M$. The operator takes the form $L = -\Delta + q - \lambda_1 q$, where $q$ is continuous on $M$, $\lambda_1$ denotes the first eigenvalue of $-\Delta + q$ subject to zero Dirichlet boundary conditions, and $\Delta$ represents the Laplace–Beltrami operator. We establish the existence of a positive, bounded ground state for $L$ provided $\partial M$ is a smooth hypersurface with constant mean curvature. Furthermore, we demonstrate that if $\partial M$ is replaced by a compact domain $\Omega$ containing it in its interior, the concentration parameter $\lambda$ must be adjusted to maintain the boundedness of the ground state.

This study examines the application of direct regression as a methodology for camera calibration. The process involves training a deep learning regression model to output intrinsic parameters by directly processing a single image. The training dataset consists of synthetic data, where the training distribution is constructed from the statistics of the corresponding ground truth values derived from real images. The efficacy of this approach is evaluated using a database of 1,000 images sourced from the Microsoft COVHO3D dataset. The results indicate that this distribution is highly effective, yielding a training Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.17 for the training data. When evaluated on unseen test images, the prototype achieved a test RMSE of 0.24, surpassing the performance of classical calibration algorithms. Furthermore, the 95% confidence intervals for the estimated values were notably narrower than those produced by classical methods, suggesting a significant reduction in uncertainty. The computational cost for calibration is minimal, requiring approximately 100 milliseconds per image on a single GPU. The approach is highly versatile, remaining robust despite the use of data with a broad range of noise levels and the inclusion of only synthetic training data. Additionally, the method is easily extendable to scenarios with multiple cameras or the joint calibration of cameras and sensors.

We introduce a regularized conditional Wasserstein GAN (cWGAN) designed to generate high-quality, diverse, and approximately uncorrelated samples from a target distribution conditioned on specific inputs. This approach leverages the Implicit Filtering Markov Chain Monte Carlo (IF-MCMC) framework to transform conditional Wilson–GAN sampling into an effective method for producing nearly independent conditional target samples. We formalize the implicit relationship between implicit sampling iterations and IF-MCMC steps to demonstrate convergence toward the desired conditional distribution, explicitly defining the necessary range for the GAN loss gradient norm. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between the GAN's implicit mapping and the solution of a specific optimal control problem, utilizing this insight to shape the generator's architecture. Empirical evaluations across various benchmarks confirm the efficacy of our technique in generating diverse and largely independent conditional output samples.

This paper investigates the characterization of linear subspaces that remain invariant within system descriptions of fractional order. It establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for invariant subspace invariance specific to fully distributed and strictly causal models. Additionally, it explores the relationship between these subspaces and the system's poles. The core approach involves representing the systems via a Riemann-Liouville fractional integral operator and applying calculus techniques to establish results for fully distributed and strictly causal cases. Ultimately, this work offers mathematical insights intended to support the practical design of controllers within systems of fractional order.

This paper introduces a technique for establishing multi-hop terahertz (THz) links that minimizes the amount of beam training required. The proposed dynamic beam training approach adapts its strategy based on the current network configuration and the specific conditions of the channel. A key innovation is the utilization of a "superbeam," which combines several narrow beams to cover a broader area, thereby reducing the number of training steps needed at both transmitter and receiver. Furthermore, the research examines a scenario where intermediate relays can exchange channel feedback information. Under these premises, the total communication throughput across the relay chain is evaluated and compared against a traditional method that operates independently of feedback dynamics. The findings indicate that the proposed dynamic beam training strategy significantly boosts throughput in multi-hop THz environments by halving the beam training overhead relative to the conventional approach.

Pulsar B1133+16, located 1.1 kiloparsecs away, has been observed for 11 years using the Arecibo and Green Bank radio telescopes. Analysis of these observations reveals that the pulsar signal traverses at least 11 distinct scattering screens, a conclusion supported by examining temporal broadening, scintillation, and the statistical distribution of burst events. These findings indicate scattering measures ranging from 1.3 to 10.3 $\times 10^{-18}$ $\rm m}^2$ and screen distances between 1.3 and 56 astronomical units (AU) relative to Earth. The presence of screens at both 1.3 and 56 AU suggests scattering mechanisms similar to those found in the Galactic Disk, yet the majority of screens situated between roughly 2 and 50 AU implies widespread scattering structures within the Galactic Bulge, which dominates the scattering effects for this nearby pulsar. Additionally, the data includes detailed measurements of electron content within each screen.

Although deep neural networks have achieved significant success in speech recognition and synthesis, their application has been hindered by an inability to model the quasi-periodic characteristics of speech. This limitation stems largely from the assumption of statistical independence between samples in the standard feed-forward architecture. To address this, we propose a Long-Short Term Recurrent Neural Network (L-STRNN) designed to capture both the stationary and non-stationary features of acoustic waveforms. The proposed method employs a recurrent network structure that integrates a fixed filter bank to extract stationary properties and a variable filter with fixed phase locking to capture locking mechanisms. We evaluated the L-STRNN on the LDC's Corpus of Quasi-Periodic Speech (CQPS) for quasi-locking classification and on the CQPS and AMI Meeting Assistants for quasi-syntactic tagging. Results indicate that the model effectively learns the concept of speech locking across both quasi-stationary quasi-periodic signals and the more complex, varying quasi-synchronous syntactic patterns found in meetings.

Annotators often face challenges maintaining consistency and focus when labeling attention on massive text documents. To address this, we introduce a tool that converts text into annotated graphical representations, enabling annotators to review data more effectively and concentrate on labeling rather than scrolling. We illustrate the utility of this approach by introducing "RelationGraph," which transforms abstract dependency graphs into an accessible visual interface. RelationalGraph allows annotators to interact with visualized natural language inference (NL) datasets, shifting their focus from navigating text to analyzing the associated dependency structures. Evaluations indicate that using such annotations improves annotator productivity. Furthermore, we report on a crowdsourcing study demonstrating that this method yields performance comparable to standard text-based labeling techniques.

This study utilizes the Exoplanet Characterisation Environment (E-PEC) to model how a temperate planet's atmospheric metallicity influences its composition and appearance. We examined the effects of varying metallicity on the mixing ratios of key chemical species, including H$_2$, He, CO, CO$_2$, H$_2$O, CH$_4$, and NH$_3$. Our models indicate that at low temperatures (~300 K), a 0.1-bar atmosphere shifts from being hydrogen-dominated to one dominated by volatiles when metallicity reaches $10^{-5}$ times the total atmospheric mass. Furthermore, we explored the interplay between low gravity ($1~\text{m s}^{-2}$) and high atmospheric enrichment ($10^{-4}$), demonstrating that such conditions generate unique, metallicity-driven atmospheric patches where volatile concentrations are elevated by orders of magnitude. These conditions significantly alter the planet's visual appearance, resulting in extensive regions dominated by colourless CO and CO$_2$ alongside distinct ammonia clouds, which are absent in standard atmospheric models.

This study proposes a novel method for inspecting and maintaining urban road surfaces using a single mobile LiDAR scanner. The proposed approach aims to automate the creation of 3D road models, an essential step in analyzing road conditions. The method relies on two key innovations: (1) RoadAtlas, an efficient representation of 2D horizontal road maps, and (2) a synchronization algorithm that aligns LiDAR scans with the vehicle's GPS location. By leveraging these components, the method successfully generates detailed 3D road models using only one mobile LiDAR sensor, streamlining the initial phase of data analysis for maintenance professionals. This streamlining is particularly significant given the massive volume of data collected during automated city-wide surveys. Our approach effectively automates the initial processing of such data, an outcome validated by a field test conducted on a standard production vehicle equipped with a single LiDAR unit. The test covered 14.5 kilometers of road in Los Angeles, demonstrating accurate GPS synchronization over the distance and achieving a processing time of 1.5 hours for the resulting point cloud dataset.

We demonstrate that the bicategorical topological shadow of a bicategorical $G$-space precisely recovers the bicategorical topological Hochschild homology (tHH) of the associated tHH-$G$-module, thereby generalizing the findings in [10]. Additionally, we present computational techniques for bicategorical tHH applicable to specific $G$-groups of interest, an advancement that overcomes limitations encountered in the classical topological Hochschild homology tHH-G-group context.

At VGG-Sound Source (VGG-SS), we present a benchmark for sound source classification that includes 1,000 professionally annotated, high-quality audio clips sourced from the internet. Designed to improve upon current benchmarks, VGG-SS offers broader topic diversity, improved data balance, and a larger variety of background noise. Our analysis indicates that the benchmark's robustness is further ensured by its resilience to background interference; consequently, we report new state-of-the-art classification results using several trained classifiers.

Graph neural networks have recently emerged as a powerful tool for node classification tasks on graphs defined by Euclidean geometry. Nevertheless, their application to graphs with hyperbolic geometry remains limited, largely due to the scarcity of suitable graph aggregations that respect the negative curvature required by hyperbolic spaces. We propose the Graph Neural Network, a method that leverages the Poincaré ball model of hyperbolic geometry to address this issue. Our approach utilizes the fact that the Laplace operator in hyperbolic spaces can be expressed as a weighted sum of Laplace operators in Euclidean spaces to create a graph aggregation scheme. This results in a node classification algorithm that is both simple to implement and computationally efficient. Extensive experiments on various hyperbolic graphs demonstrate that LGCN outperforms existing state-of-the-art hyperbolic graph neural networks.

This work derives new stability findings for the inverse obstacle problem within the framework of time-dependent Navier-Stokes equations. The approach relies on an appropriate observation inequality and the application of the Rellich-Rosenbloom-Cauchy inequalities. A foundational element of the method involves establishing a specific input-output inequality, which connects a perturbation in pressure to normal fluid velocities on an obstacle. The derivation of this inequality is not self-evident and necessitates the use of enhanced test functions; it demands a meticulous analysis of the Navier-Stokes structure and leverages full observability to ensure validity. Ultimately, the presence of an obstacle influences both the nonlinear terms in the Navier-Stokes formulation and its nonlinear boundary conditions, factors that are accounted for in the results. Consequently, the derived observability inequality facilitates comprehensive observations regarding various stability outcomes, covering uniqueness in determining the shape of the non-penetrable barrier, stability in identifying normal velocities on such obstacles, and uniqueness in identifying a rigid stationary body.

Tunneling spectroscopy is a powerful technique for imaging electronic band structures, yet its optical counterpart remains elusive. We demonstrate that Tavis-Schriefer tunneling spectroscopy (TSS) can be realized in a coupled optomechanical system. This optical TSS arises when a single optical cavity interacts with two mechanically resonators, where one is frozen and the other is vibrational. By utilizing the Poincare-Langevin equation, we derived that the fluorescence spectrum exhibits a distinct anti-crossing feature, confirming the TSS effect. The anti-crossing can be observed even when the mechanical frequencies differ, and its characteristics can be tuned by mechanical dissipation or coupling strengths. Notably, this effect persists regardless of whether the optomechanical interactions are linear or nonlinear. Furthermore, we show that linking the mechanical modes to the same cavity allows the TSS signature to endure across a broad spectrum, regardless of whether the resonator modes operate in the red- or blue-detuned regimes relative to the optical frequency.

This paper explores the application of the atoms from the $\tau$-calculus within an automata-theoretic framework. We present a novel, Fariyian-style construction that links the satisfaction of any $\tau$-net with respect to a $\tau$-term to the acceptance of a specific automaton by a corresponding tree language. This construction leverages the expressive limitations inherent in the absence of modalities within $\tau$-terms, which in turn establishes new results regarding satisfiability and the undecidability questions of $\tau$-net equivalence and satisfaction for finite sets of $t$-terms.

The Tsallis distribution, frequently utilized to fit empirical data across diverse fields, warrants a deeper understanding of its underlying mechanisms. While statistical mechanics provides a robust derivation through the maximum entropy principle, this approach necessitates specifying an appropriate probability measure. In the context of social systems, we demonstrate that the Lebesgue measure naturally yields the Tsallis distribution when applied within a social analog of the maximum entropy principle. Furthermore, we argue that the critical free parameter in the Tsallis fit represents the degree of system clustering. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our framework by analyzing the geographic distribution of cities in the United States.

The visual assessment and management of colorectal adenomas rely heavily on skilled endoscopists, a process often hindered by human limitations such as fatigue and reduced sensitivity in detecting early lesions. Recently, deep neural networks have demonstrated significant potential in the classification and grading of colorectal adenocarcinoma through studies using synthetic image collections. This study introduces an alternative strategy employing actual endoscopic video footage to train a deep neural network for the detection and characterization of colorectal polyps. Specifically, we employed a ResNet-101 architecture trained on images manually cropped from videos, supplemented by an attention mechanism designed to enhance performance with lower-resolution depictions of polyps. Furthermore, a data augmentation technique was utilized to mitigate potential biases arising from the one-shot learning nature of the approach. The proposed method was evaluated on a dataset comprising videos sourced from a single endoscopy unit, featuring 586 adenomatous polyps and 15,245 corresponding images. Evaluation metrics included a ResNet-101 model trained on image-level data and ablation studies comparing various augmentation strategies, video classification performance, and the specific impact of the attention mechanism on overall outcomes.

This study introduces a novel high-order hybrid Discontinuous Galerkin (HG-DG) method designed for solving high-frequency acoustic scattering problems involving sound-soft obstacles. The approach constructs the total acoustic field as the sum of an incoming wave and a local unknown component restricted only to a small neighborhood around the obstacle. By formulating the problem within this reduced domain, the traditional exterior domain is eliminated, transforming the original infinite region into a bounded computational area. The design of the proposed scheme integrates two key elements: a fully high-order perturbed interior DG method applied within this restricted domain and a specially crafted high-order boundary condition. This boundary condition leverages a high-order multipole expansion of the incoming wave alongside a high-order boundary condition derived from the far-field condition to approximate the original physical boundary conditions at a significantly higher order. Numerical experiments conducted at extremely high frequencies demonstrate the method's efficiency, demonstrating that it achieves significantly greater efficiency compared to conventional exterior DG methods by requiring fewer degrees of freedom to reach a specified level of accuracy.

This study analyzes the water content of ordinary chondrite Antarctic samples discovered in the Ensenada del Castillo region, located in the northern part of the International Divide Region (IDR). Utilizing near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy, we determined that these finds contain approximately 0.2% water by weight, a level comparable to recent ordinary chondrite falls Benenitra and Chelyabinsk, which share similar low-temperature alteration histories. Spectroscopic findings indicate that these finds exhibit a spectral signature consistent with hydrated phyllosilicates containing an estimated 10–15% clay-bound water. Furthermore, these finds exhibit spectral characteristics closely resembling those of the ordinary chondrite parent asteroid Ryugu observed by the Hayabusa2 mission. These results suggest that ordinary chondrite meteorites from the IDR contain a substantial reservoir of water that could have been available for incorporation into early planetary bodies.

The multipole decomposition of electromagnetic radiation serves as a fundamental tool in classical electrodynamics, with electric dipole and magnetostatic approximations frequently employed to model systems like light-matter interactions and antenna theory. While the conventional choice of multipoles relies on a gauge-dependent vector potential lacking a unique physical basis, this paper investigates alternative electric and magnetic multipole definitions using electric and magnetic fields alone. The analysis highlights that the well-known Chew expansion is capable of electric-magnetic symmetry, whereas the Pancharatskhy scheme yields primarily electric multipoles with minor magnetic contributions. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the CST (Chew-Schwinger) expansion provides a superior balanced electric-magnetic multipole mixture compared to previous methods. Finally, the research argues that the CST multipoles constitute a superior general framework for describing electromagnetic scattering.

This paper demonstrates that the Schur elements appearing in the Harish-Chandra isomorphism for the affine Hecke algebra of type $A_n$ at generic parameters effectively become *shifted Schur polynomials* (evaluated at a specific Hecke-chambers parameter set) once restricted to any affine Weyl orbit within the isomorphism domain. By explicitly formulating the restricted domain of the Harish-Chandra isomorphism in terms of Weyl group actions, we derive a closed formula for the inverse restriction, showing that both operations are computable via explicit polynomial expressions involving the divided power action of the Weyl group and the Hecke-algebra action. These findings are subsequently leveraged to derive a novel derivation formula for the Drinfeld-Sokolov (DS) map applicable to type $A_{n}$ Kac-Vdovik (KV) hierarchies. We further propose a conjectured formula for the DS-map in arbitrary Lie type, extending these results to general settings.

This work introduces a straightforward model for estimating spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in transition metal oxides, incorporating the influences of crystal field splitting and inter-electronic interactions. We demonstrate that the SOC strength is intrinsically linked to these parameters, yielding a result that generally deviates from the atomic SOC value. Additionally, we present a closed-form analytical solution for the model within the limit of strong correlations.

This work investigates toric complete intersection spaces as smooth submanifolds, examining how their relative $I$-functions connect via standard toric complete intersection rules and through smooth divisors. As an application, we establish the interrelation of relative $I$-functions for pairs consisting of toric complete intersections and all smooth toric divisors within them. Additionally, we outline a computational algorithm for deriving these relative $I$-functions.

Diffusion models have emerged as a powerful tool for generating medical images, yet their capacity for steerable augmentation remains limited. This study investigates conditional generation using stable diffusion, focusing on how latent code modifications influence the depiction of disease states within generated images. Our findings reveal that diffusion architectures possess an inherent ordering in their latent code conditions, where specific segments correspond to distinct levels of pathology. Leveraging this insight, we developed a novel module designed to isolate disease-related features from the latent code through frequency-domain operations. Furthermore, we introduced a new module that reorganizes these features to create a continuous, gradual transition of disease severity. Collectively, these innovations enable effective generation of conditions at varying levels without requiring retraining or data fine-tuning. Evaluations across three distinct datasets demonstrate that these methods significantly surpass current state-of-the-art techniques for latent code manipulation. Consequently, these user-friendly tools facilitate the creation of diverse, realistic medical images tailored for use in deep learning training.

"Many data experts and end-users rely on visualization tools to analyze and comprehend high-dimensional data. However, existing solutions are often too complex, requiring specialized training to use. To address this, we introduce "HiRT," a new system that makes dimensionality inspection accessible to all users through an intuitive interface. "HiRT" leverages the t-SNE algorithm and parallel coordinate plots to render data across multiple views simultaneously. By employing RGB color channels to encode distinct t-SNE hyperparameters, the system generates parameter-space visualizations that guide users in exploring different views by simply navigating through colors. As users traverse these views, the corresponding t-SNE projections update dynamically in real time. To further enhance interactivity, we have implemented data-driven camera controls that automate view transitions. Evaluation across diverse datasets demonstrates that this approach effectively supports efficient data inspection compared to traditional methods."

This study proposes a novel method for approximating smooth functions on unstructured mesh elements using a high-order 2-D monomial representation. Coefficients for this representation are determined via a least-squares procedure, employing a higher-degree polynomial to ensure a uniform fit across the entire mesh element rather than relying on local interpolants. While a closed-form solution exists for triangular elements, solving the associated system of equations numerically is necessary for elements with four or more vertices due to potential system ill-conditioning. To address this, various matrix solution techniques were evaluated and compared. Furthermore, a new approach utilizing a Cholesky decomposition of a transformed system matrix is introduced, demonstrating superior accuracy and stability relative to standard methods. The research confirms the accuracy of this technique through applications involving both triangular and higher-order polygonal elements.
